text:
arya: FYI seeing a small but reproducible latency/accuracy wobble when AWQ-int8 + prefix KV cache + continuous batching are all on.
kai: can you paste the perf window? is it tail latency or median?
mira: sounds like queueing/backpressure + stale prefix hits, seen that before with mixed quant models.
arya: median stays fine, p95 jumps ~40-60ms when under medium QPS. accuracy delta tiny (~0.6% on eval set) but correlated with reduced kv_hit_rate.
seb: interesting — reduced hit rate could change token prefixes and cause different quantized activations, small quality shift.
arya: reproduced locally with harness: toggle prefix_cache=true + batch_max_wait_ms=20 + continuous_batching=on -> hit_rate drops 7% and p95 spikes.
perf-bot: [auto] recorded run 2026-03-18T12:02Z: batch_window=20ms, qps=220, kv_hit_rate=0.81, p95=240ms
kai: can you dump the batching queue sizes and kv cache version at the same time? might be a race where cache invalidation + late-arriving requests get different prefixes.
arya: attached snippet I ran:
```
# reproduce
MODEL=llm-7b-awq-int8
BATCH_WAIT_MS=20
CONT_BATCH=1
./run_inference_harness --model $MODEL --qps 200 --batch_wait_ms $BATCH_WAIT_MS --continuous_batching $CONT_BATCH --enable_prefix_cache
```
mira: can you also try batch_wait_ms=8 and 12? if smaller window maybe avoids mixing stale cache state.
arya: did 8ms -> p95 back to baseline, kv_hit_rate recovered to 0.88, accuracy delta disappears. 12ms was a partial improvement.
seb: that suggests queueing delay is allowing cache entries to be evicted or recompiled between request arrival and batch commit.
kai: timeline theory: request A gets enqueued; meanwhile cache eviction or quantized kernel warmup happens; when batch fires, some requests use new kernel/kv-version, others old -> inconsistent internal state -> slight quality jitter.
mira: plan:
- add metrics: batch_composition.(kv_version_histogram, kernel_variant_histogram)
- log queue depth per-shard and per-tenant at batch commit
- run A/B with batch_wait_ms=10 vs 20 for 48h on shadow traffic
- if confirmed, add fast-path: if batch mixes kv_versions, prefer small immediate flush or split batches by kv_version
arya: quick patch idea (pseudo):
```
if detect_mixed_kv_versions(batch):
  split_batch_by(kv_version)
  or set batch.deadline = now()
```
perf-bot: created ticket INF-7892: "batch-kv-version-mismatch instrumentation + split policy" assigned to eng-ml
seb: also check continuous_batching coalescer logic — it may be aggregating across tiny time windows; a stricter coalesce key that includes kv_version might help.
arya: I'll run the 48h shadow with 10ms vs 20ms, + enable detailed batch logs for first 6 hours. will post plots.
kai: thanks. if we see increased cost due to smaller windows we can try selective split only when kv_version entropy > threshold.
mira: :thumbsup: good incremental approach.
arya: posting initial dashboard link once done: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/quant-batch-248765 (shadow run)
seb: keep an eye on tail token generation failures too, sometimes misaligned KV leads to decode stalls.
arya: noted — will include failure counts in report.
